correctness.rationale: On every bounded complete support trajectory, variation of constants gives \(y(t)=\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-(t-u)}x(u)^2\,du>0\); equality would force a backward half-orbit with \(x=0\) and \(\dot z=1\), contradicting boundedness. An arbitrary antiderivative test in \(x\) gives \(\mathbb E[yz\mid x]=-a\). The unchanged \(y\)- and \(z\)-equations give \(\mathbb E[y]=\mathbb E[x^2]\) and \(\mathbb E[x]=1/4\), so \(D=\mathbb E[(1-4x)^2]=16\operatorname{Var}(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[y]=(1+D)/16\). Dividing \(\mathbb E[yz]=-a\) by this positive mean yields the exact weighted-height law. The case \(D=0\) forces the unique equilibrium by invariant-support tangency and bounded completeness; strict excursion consequences follow from the weighted mean lying strictly between \(-16a\) and zero.

value.rationale: The defining feature of the Wang–Chen model is coexistence of nontrivial recurrence with a stable equilibrium, and the 2013 source demonstrates simultaneous point, periodic, and strange attractors at \(a=0.01\). The accepted theorem gives an exact stationary diagnostic tied directly to that feature: the y-weighted height of every non-equilibrium compact stationary state is forced strictly away from the stable-equilibrium height toward zero by the kinetic defect \(\mathbb E[\dot z^2]\). It also localizes the constant forcing in every represented x-fiber through \(\mathbb E[yz\mid x]=-a\). These constraints apply uniformly to periodic and chaotic invariant measures and give exact consistency checks for numerical hidden-attractor data.
